# Platform settings · Logs & privacy

## Consume logs

<a id="LogConsumeEnabled"></a>

### Consume logs

Key `LogConsumeEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Consume logs

Write a consume log for every charged request: user, API key, model, tokens, cost, channel and timing. When off no new records are written and charging goes on as before, but the log list, the usage statistics built from logs and per-user histories have a gap. Top-ups, sign-up bonuses and other system logs are written either way.

See also: [Delete old consume logs](./privacy.md#LogAutoDeleteEnabled) · [Allow keeping request bodies](./privacy.md#LogIOEnabled)

<a id="LogRelayErrorEnabled"></a>

### Log failed requests

Key `LogRelayErrorEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Consume logs

Write an error log when a request still fails after its retries, with the error the client got and every channel tried. Requests refused locally (insufficient quota, invalid parameters) are not logged.

<a id="ChannelMetricsEnabled"></a>

### Hourly channel metrics

Key `ChannelMetricsEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Consume logs

Count attempts, successes, latency, time to first token and output speed per channel, model and hour. The counters are kept in memory, written every minute and read through GET /api/channel/metrics. When off nothing new is counted; stored hours stay until they expire.

See also: [Keep metrics for (days)](./privacy.md#ChannelMetricsRetentionDays)

<a id="ChannelMetricsRetentionDays"></a>

### Keep metrics for (days)

Key `ChannelMetricsRetentionDays` · Type int · Unit days · Range 0– · Default `30`

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Consume logs

How many days of hourly channel metrics are kept; older hours are deleted every night at 03:10 server time. 0 keeps them forever.

Examples:

- `30` The default: at most 30 x 24 = 720 rows per channel and model.
- `0` Nothing is deleted: the table grows by one row per channel, model and hour in use.

See also: [Hourly channel metrics](./privacy.md#ChannelMetricsEnabled)

<a id="LogAutoDeleteEnabled"></a>

### Delete old consume logs

Key `LogAutoDeleteEnabled` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Consume logs

Delete consume logs older than the retention days every night at 03:00 server time, with their kept bodies. Error and system logs stay, and so do the daily usage statistics already built from the deleted logs.

See also: [Keep consume logs for (days)](./privacy.md#LogAutoDeleteDays) · [Consume logs](./privacy.md#LogConsumeEnabled)

<a id="LogAutoDeleteDays"></a>

### Keep consume logs for (days)

Key `LogAutoDeleteDays` · Type int · Unit days · Range 0– · Default `30`

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Consume logs

How many days of consume logs are kept when old logs are deleted automatically. Older logs go in the nightly cleanup; 0 deletes nothing.

Examples:

- `30` The default: a month of logs is kept; a log written on 1 May is gone by 1 June.
- `90` A quarter is kept, about three times the rows of the default.

See also: [Delete old consume logs](./privacy.md#LogAutoDeleteEnabled)

## Request & response retention

<a id="LogIOEnabled"></a>

### Allow keeping request bodies

Key `LogIOEnabled` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Request & response retention

Site-wide switch for keeping the full request and response bodies of API calls, for troubleshooting. When off (the default, zero data retention) no API key keeps them and the option is hidden from personal and organization settings. When on, each user's or organization's own choice decides, and the defaults for personal and organization API keys apply until they choose. Bodies are cut at 1 MB each by default, kept 30 days, and never include API keys or auth headers.

See also: [Default for personal API keys](./privacy.md#LogIODefaultUser) · [Default for organization API keys](./privacy.md#OrganizationLogIODefault)

<a id="LogIODefaultUser"></a>

### Default for personal API keys

Key `LogIODefaultUser` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Request & response retention

Whether personal API keys keep request and response bodies while their user has not chosen. Users can change it any time in their personal settings. Needs Allow keeping request bodies.

See also: [Allow keeping request bodies](./privacy.md#LogIOEnabled) · [Default for organization API keys](./privacy.md#OrganizationLogIODefault)

<a id="OrganizationLogIODefault"></a>

### Default for organization API keys

Key `OrganizationLogIODefault` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Request & response retention

Whether organization API keys keep request and response bodies while the organization has not chosen. Organization admins can change it in the organization settings. Needs Allow keeping request bodies.

See also: [Allow keeping request bodies](./privacy.md#LogIOEnabled) · [Default for personal API keys](./privacy.md#LogIODefaultUser)

## Content safety

<a id="EnableSafe"></a>

### Content safety check

Key `EnableSafe` · Type bool · Default `false`

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Content safety

Check the text of every request with the safety tool before it goes to a channel, and refuse matches with a 400 error. Messages, system prompts, tool definitions and the client events of Realtime and Gemini Live sessions are checked; images and audio are not.

See also: [Safety tool](./privacy.md#SafeToolName) · [Blocked keywords](./privacy.md#SafeKeyWords)

<a id="SafeToolName"></a>

### Safety tool

Key `SafeToolName` · Type enum · Default `Keyword` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Content safety

The tool that runs the content safety check. Keyword is the one built in. A tool that is not installed refuses every request.

Values:

- `Keyword` Keyword: Refuses requests whose text contains a word of the blocked keywords.

See also: [Content safety check](./privacy.md#EnableSafe) · [Blocked keywords](./privacy.md#SafeKeyWords)

<a id="SafeKeyWords"></a>

### Blocked keywords

Key `SafeKeyWords` · Type list

Where: Platform settings › Logs & privacy › Content safety

The words the Keyword tool blocks, one per line. A request is refused when its text contains any of them, ignoring case, also inside longer words. Empty lines are ignored.

Examples:

- `casino` Refuses "Plan a casino night" and "best casinos".
- `ass` Also refuses "class" and "password": short words match inside longer ones, so list whole, unusual words.

See also: [Content safety check](./privacy.md#EnableSafe) · [Safety tool](./privacy.md#SafeToolName)
